newsitem.title: FRANCE: French firms to invest in new Calais sugar silo.
newsitem.headline: French firms to invest in new Calais sugar silo.

text.p: French sugar exporter and silo operator Transit Stockage Manutention (TSM) said on Wednesday two of its shareholders, Union des Sucreries et Distilleries Agricoles (SDA) and Beghin-Say, will invest in a new 60,000 tonnes sugar storage facility in the northern port of Calais.
"SDA and Beghin-Say will invest in the silo and TSM will be the operator," TSM deputy director Franck Degouy told Reuters.
The 55 milllion francs plant will start operations in October.
SDA already owns some 20 percent of TSM and Beghin-Say one percent. Other TSM shareholders include large sugar operators such as Sucre Export Anvers and SHGT.

TSM has operated a sugar terminal in Calais since 1995, including a 7,000 tonnes silo. But because of limited storage capacity the group has lost business to nearby ports such as Antwerp in Belgium and Dunkirk in northern France, Degouy said.
TSM handled 300,000 tonnes of sugar last year and hopes to process at least as much this year.
